verifier_note: Verified by retrieval (never memory): all 49 warrant-source rows across 36 unique URLs resolved and supported their claims, including 3 cases where rustdoc HTML was too large for the fetch tool and I fell back to the actual rustc/std source at the pinned 1.98.1 git tag for ground truth (Termination's Result impl, strict_abs, wrapping_shl). Engine facts were checked read-only against mcp-tool-shop-org/si-rpg-engine main (function names, the single unwrap() at rapier_law.rs:561, Cargo.toml profile flags, and a git diff of commit 6a33297 confirming the continue->return false change) and all matched exactly. All 46 checks in this lane were executed with scripts/compile_oracle.py against the pinned rustc 1.98.1 on this Windows rig and passed with zero mismatches, including host-specific values like the 3221226505 (0xC0000409) abort exit code; I also independently reproduced the 'immediate-abort requires nightly' rejection verbatim. Zero refutations and zero corrections were needed. The one systemic weakness: engine_note claims mix durable anchors (function/constant names, which most recipes correctly use) with a fragile one -- recipe 4 cites an exact source line number pinned to a single commit, in a repo that took two more commits within the same day of this sweep. It still holds at current HEAD, but nothing in the lane structure would catch silent line-number drift on the next unrelated edit above that line. Recipe 6 is marked 'plausible' rather than 'solid' because one prose detail (Node's exact 'RuntimeError: unreachable' trap text) rests on the W3C spec's weaker guarantee (an unspecified-message RuntimeError) rather than a source or execution I could confirm verbatim, and its one background source predates 2021.
